extracted.intended_audience: general readers and mathematicians (including AMS members)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the scope, content types, editorial practices, publication frequency, and audience of the membership journal 'Notices of the American Mathematical Society'. Useful for understanding what kinds of pieces the journal publishes and how it is produced/distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expository research articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Each issue of the Notices contains one or two expository articles describing current developments in mathematical research, written by professional mathematicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These pieces are intended to be expository (accessible summaries/explanations) about current developments; typically there are one or two per issue and authors are professional mathematicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: History, education, and professional-issues articles
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal also carries articles on the history of mathematics, mathematics education, and professional issues facing mathematicians, along with reviews of books, plays, movies, and other artistic and cultural works involving mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions in these topic areas are within the Notices' scope and may take the form of feature articles or reviews; the journal presents a broad set of mathematical-cultural content beyond pure research exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular columns
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular columns include Math Reviews News, Washington Update on policy matters affecting mathematicians, and Short Stories exploring lesser-known mathematical results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notices maintains standing columns with focused purposes: news about reviews, policy updates relevant to the community, and short expositions of interesting/obscure results. Contributions aligned with these column themes are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Career section
rubrics_metrics.description: The Early Career section provides advice to graduate students, postdocs, and junior mathematicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material offering career advice, professional development, and guidance targeted to early-career mathematicians is an explicit and recurring component of the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review by editorial board
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are peer reviewed by an editorial board of mathematical experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are subject to editorial peer review by experts; this indicates standards of scholarly vetting and selection by the journal's editorial board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover features mathematical visualizations
rubrics_metrics.description: The cover regularly features mathematical visualizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal emphasizes visual/math-artistic content on its cover, suggesting value placed on visually engaging mathematical representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication frequency and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Published monthly, except combined June/July issue; distributed to approximately 30,000 AMS members worldwide, one-third of whom reside outside the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notices is a frequent (monthly) membership journal with wide distribution among AMS members, indicating a professional/audience expectation (broad, membership-focused readership).

rubrics_metrics.name: Online availability of issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Each issue since January 1995 is available in its entirety on the journal's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archival/online availability is part of the journal's publication model; contributors' work is publicly accessible online for back issues dating to 1995.
